evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to the CLI with tests, update the README section that lists the flags, and commit the result.
evals.expected_output: Before any work, the agent splits the request into three deliverables and routes the flag and tests to gpt-6.1-sol, the README prose to claude-opus-5-5, and the commit to gpt-6-luna, then identifies the harness and checks each selected model before starting, recording any unavailable runtime verification as an unverified route.
expectations: The agent classifies the deliverables before writing code or delegating
The flag implementation and its tests are routed to gpt-6.1-sol
The README update is routed to claude-opus-5-5 as prose shipped with a Development change, separately from the implementation
The commit is routed to gpt-6-luna
The agent identifies the current harness and resolves each model ID against its catalog before switching or launching
Each route records the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort setting or unsupported, and session identifier or none
When runtime verification is unavailable after explicit model selection, the agent records an unverified route; a failed selection or mismatched model takes the next applicable execution path
evals.baseline: Without the skill the agent did everything itself on claude-fable-5-1: it added --dry-run to cli.py, wrote five tests, extended the README Flags list, and committed as 'feat: add --dry-run flag to list files without deleting them'. It never split the request into deliverables, named no model, did not identify the harness or consult any catalog, launched no other session, and recorded no route, so every expectation about routing to gpt-6.1-sol, claude-opus-5-5, and gpt-6-luna and about route records fell short. The orchestrator seeded the workspace with a small argparse CLI, a unittest suite, and a README with a Flags section because the evaluation supplies no fixtures.

runs.notes: All expectations held. The subagent read the skill, classified the three deliverables before touching code, identified the harness as Claude Code under T3 Code on claude-fable-5-1, and, because a Claude Code subagent cannot switch its own model and the Agent tool only takes Anthropic aliases, used the external codex CLI for the OpenAI routes: flag and tests on codex session 01a114bb-a801-7291-9e36-b1d386a3fb4e (rollout metadata model gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning_effort high, confirmed by the orchestrator), help text and README bullet on an Agent sub-session with alias opus whose launch result reported claude-opus-5-5, commit on codex session 01a114bd-ddbd-7a31-a60e-2fb3468cafd1 (rollout metadata gpt-6-luna, effort high). All three routes were recorded in the skill's form with model, verification source, harness, effort, and session. The first Luna commit attempt failed because the codex workspace-write sandbox keeps .git read-only; the agent resumed the same session with the sandbox bypassed instead of changing model, and commit 2923219 'feat: add --dry-run flag' landed with README, cli.py, and tests. No route needed the unverified marker. Observation: the codex workers loaded model-routing themselves and the Sol worker spawned a child thread, also on gpt-6.1-sol.

Codex read ~/.agents/skills/model-routing/SKILL.md and stated the three routes before working, but then performed the Development part itself. Failed: 'The flag implementation and its tests are routed to gpt-6.1-sol': the gpt-6-astra exec session edited cli.py and tests/test_cli.py directly and never launched a gpt-6.1-sol session. Failed: 'The commit is routed to gpt-6-luna': no Luna session was started; the agent only noted that .git is read-only inside the workspace-write sandbox and left the changes uncommitted. Failed: 'Each route records the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort setting or unsupported, and session identifier or none': no route line in the skill's form appeared; the final message was prose ('Blocked by two issues') rather than the Blocked/Attempts/Needed report. Held: classification before work; the README was routed separately to claude-opus-5-5 via 'claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high -p', which failed with EAI_AGAIN because the codex sandbox has no network, after which the agent asked the user whether gpt-6.1-sol may write the prose instead. README unchanged, partial --dry-run in the working tree, 3 tests passing.

OpenCode loaded the skill via its Skill tool and stated the routes (implementation and tests to GPT 6.1 Sol, README and help text to Claude Opus 5.5, commit to GPT 6 Luna) before any work, then ran command -v, opencode --help, opencode models, opencode session list, codex --help, claude --help, codex login status, codex agents --help, and claude auth status. Its next two tool calls, read on /home/agent/.codex and /home/agent/.claude, were rejected by the non-interactive permission system and the session ended with finish reason tool-calls, no final message, and the workspace untouched (exit code 0). Failed: 'The flag implementation and its tests are routed to gpt-6.1-sol', 'The README update is routed to claude-opus-5-5 as prose shipped with a Development change, separately from the implementation', 'The commit is routed to gpt-6-luna': no session was launched for any deliverable and nothing was produced. Failed: 'The agent identifies the current harness and resolves each model ID against its catalog before switching or launching': it listed the opencode catalog but never resolved or launched. Failed: 'Each route records the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort setting or unsupported, and session identifier or none' and the Blocked report: no route record and no report, because the run ended silently. Held: classification before writing code or delegating.

evals.prompt: Use gpt-6-luna to write the design specification for the new cache layer, and also fix the failing test in cache_test.py.
evals.expected_output: The agent honours the user's model choice for the specification only, routes the test fix to gpt-6.1-sol, and runs each deliverable on its selected model, marking the route unverified when runtime verification is unavailable.
expectations: The specification is written on gpt-6-luna because the user chose it explicitly
The override is applied only to the specification; the test fix is routed to gpt-6.1-sol
Any escalation of the test fix to gpt-6-astra meets a Development escalation condition and is explained to the user
Each execution session has the assigned model explicitly selected, with runtime verification or a recorded verification gap
If no execution path reaches a model, the agent reports the attempted harnesses and failures and asks the user to provide access or choose an available model
When reusing a session, including a focused follow-up or external CLI session, the agent checks every suitability criterion before resuming it
evals.baseline: Without the skill the agent honoured the explicit model choice for the specification by calling 'opencode run -m openai/gpt-6-luna' from Bash, which wrote docs/cache-layer-design.md, and fixed the failing test_get_refreshes_recency itself on claude-fable-5-1 by adding move_to_end to LRUCache.get. It never classified the deliverables or routed the test fix to gpt-6.1-sol, did not identify the harness, verified no model from session metadata, checked no session for reuse, and recorded no route; the opencode worker also briefly reverted the fix because its handoff did not fence off cache.py, and the agent reapplied it. The orchestrator seeded the workspace with cache.py and a cache_test.py whose recency test fails because the evaluation supplies no fixtures.

runs.notes: All expectations held. The subagent split the task in two, identified the harness as Claude Code under T3 Code on claude-fable-5-1, noted that a Claude Code subagent cannot switch its own model and that the Agent tool accepts only Anthropic models, and used the external codex CLI: the specification on session 01a114ba-f955-7763-90a9-c484714be49c (rollout metadata model gpt-6-luna, effort high, recorded as the user's override of the Fable route) and the test fix on session 01a114bb-0fbf-7122-8fec-4e2e6c564cef (rollout metadata gpt-6.1-sol, effort high), both confirmed by the orchestrator. No escalation to gpt-6-astra. Both routes were recorded in the skill's form with the launch header as verification source. The Luna worker loaded model-routing itself and first reported Blocked because the handoff omitted the user's explicit model choice; the agent resumed that same session with the override stated, a reuse of its own idle session on the same repository, topic, and model. Results: cache.py gained move_to_end in get, 3 tests pass, docs/cache-layer-spec.md written, nothing committed.

evals.prompt: Restructure the service layer across all four packages so they share one repository interface, and label the issues that came in overnight.
evals.expected_output: The agent escalates the cross-package refactor to gpt-6-astra with an explanation, routes the labelling to gpt-6-luna, and sends any defect the labelling uncovers back to Development.
expectations: The refactor is classified as Development and escalated to gpt-6-astra because it needs broad cross-module context
The escalation is explained to the user before the refactor starts
The issue labelling is routed to gpt-6-luna as routine triage
A defect found while labelling is treated as Development and routed to gpt-6.1-sol
If a model not found error occurs, the agent checks the catalog and retries only with a newly verified identifier or setting; otherwise it proceeds to the next applicable path
evals.baseline: Without the skill the agent did both parts itself on claude-fable-5-1: it wrote packages/repository.py with a Repository protocol and InMemoryRepository, rewired all four services to constructor injection, deleted the three package-specific stores, extended the tests, and labelled issues #3 to #6 in grauzone-dev/skill-evals with enhancement, documentation, and good first issue via gh. It never classified the refactor as Development, did not escalate to gpt-6-astra or explain any escalation, did not route the labelling to gpt-6-luna, launched no other session, and recorded no route. The orchestrator built the workspace from a clone of grauzone-dev/skill-evals (live tracker with four unlabelled issues from 2026-10-06) plus four locally committed service packages with divergent storage access, because the evaluation supplies no fixtures.

runs.notes: Failed: 'The escalation is explained to the user before the refactor starts': the subagent's only text before launching the refactor was 'Ich lade zuerst den model-routing-Skill'; it then ran codex exec -m gpt-6-astra for the refactor and codex exec -m gpt-6-luna for the labelling in the same step, and the explanation (cross-package architecture refactor needs broad module context, hence Astra instead of GPT 6.1 Sol) appeared only in the final report after both workers had finished. A subagent can still emit text before a launch, so the limitation is partial. Every other expectation held: the refactor was classified as Development and ran on codex session 01a114c8-0ec1-7823-bd04-17d8f0f78222 (rollout metadata model gpt-6-astra, effort high); the labelling ran on codex session 01a114c8-320c-7aa0-9624-97ab208aa647 as routine triage and applied enhancement, good first issue, and documentation to #3 to #6 only, leaving the issues #12 to #17 that another process created during the run untouched; no defect surfaced among those four, so the Development hand-back was not exercised; no model-not-found error occurred, but the first 'codex exec resume' ran on the default gpt-6.1-sol without network, the agent read that from the header, and retried only with the verified -m gpt-6-luna and effort config. The packages/README.md prose was first bundled into the Astra handoff, which Astra paused as not its deliverable, and was then routed to an Agent sub-session on claude-opus-5-5; three routes were recorded in the skill's form. A Claude Code subagent cannot switch its own model, so all OpenAI routes used the external codex fallback. Refactor result: shared Repository ABC with get, save, list, per-package in-memory repositories, 16 tests passing, nothing committed; the orchestrator removed the labels afterwards to restore the sandbox.
